svg.title: Kisspeptin: what has actually been tested
svg.desc: Kisspeptin: what has actually been tested. Cancer gene (1996): Found as a melanoma metastasis-suppressor gene in Hershey, Pennsylvania. Verdict: Lab finding. Puberty switch (2003): Broken receptor gene means no puberty in families and mice. Verdict: Established. Single dose raises LH and testosterone: Small supervised studies in healthy men, mostly by vein. Verdict: Shown, short-term. Repeated or constant dosing: Response fades; a constant potent analog suppressed testosterone. Verdict: Response fades. Raising low testosterone (analog): Two drug-company phase 2a trials stopped for missing primary endpoints. Verdict: Not shown. Fertility after TRT or steroids: No published trials found; a 2026 review calls direct evidence limited. Verdict: No direct evidence. IVF egg-maturation trigger: Phase 2 trials in women at high risk of overstimulation. Verdict: Promising, phase 2. Libido and sexual brain response: Two 32-person crossover trials, single infusions, low desire. Verdict: Early signal. Approved product or legal compounding: None approved; FDA 503A category 2 since 2023; banned in sport. Verdict: None.
